message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of May 2026) | Area | What You’re Generally Entitled To | |------|------------------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent.
• Must return deposit within 30 days after you move out unless deductions are made for damages beyond normal wear and tear.
• Written itemized list of deductions required if anything is withheld. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlords must keep premises safe, sanitary, and fit for habitation—plumbing, heating/cooling, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.
• If repairs aren’t done promptly, you can:
 – Request repair in writing
 – Pay yourself and deduct from rent (Texas Property Code §92.006)
 – Withhold rent until repaired (but only after giving notice). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent due when specified in lease (usually monthly).
• Late fees allowed but cannot exceed $50 per day or 5% of rent, whichever is less (§91.013). | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment: 10‑day written notice before eviction proceedings.
• For termination of tenancy: 90‑days’ written notice for month‑to‑month leases; longer if lease specifies otherwise. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord must respect your right to privacy and peaceful use of rented property. Unreasonable inspections or entry without proper notice (at least 24 hours) violate this right. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Protected under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Civil Rights Act against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, age, marital status, source of income, sexual orientation, gender identity, or veteran status. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease agreements must be in writing for residential rentals over one year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “subletting”) can be challenged if they conflict with local ordinances or state law. | | **Eviction Process** | • Evictions require court action; landlord must file complaint, serve notice, attend hearing.
• Tenants have the right to contest evictions and present evidence at hearings. | | **Utilities & Maintenance Responsibilities** | • Typically split between landlord and tenant as outlined in lease.
• Landlord responsible for major systems; tenants handle minor upkeep like trash removal. | --- #### Practical Steps If Issues Arise 1. **Document Everything:** Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of damage, and maintenance requests. 2. **Written Requests First:** Send formal notices via certified mail or email (with read receipt) so there’s proof of delivery. 3. **Know Local Ordinances:** Some cities (Austin, Dallas, Houston) impose extra protections such as rent caps or mandatory mediation steps. Check city codes. 4. **Seek Mediation/Legal Aid:** Many counties offer free or low-cost housing counseling services. 5. **File Complaint:** If landlord violates habitability standards, report to the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR) or local health department. --- #### Quick Reference Checklist - [ ] Verify security deposit amount and conditions. - [ ] Confirm lease terms regarding pet rules, subleasing, utilities. - [ ] Know how much time you have to pay late rent before penalties apply. - [ ] Understand the correct procedure for requesting repairs. - [ ] Be aware of the notice period required for ending tenancy. - [ ] Keep records of all interactions with landlord. If you encounter a problem, start by reviewing your lease, then contact your landlord in writing. If unresolved, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or attorney who specializes in landlord‑tenant law.
